This slightly reduces the discovery challenge but stays within plausible engineering-comment norms and does not leak grading internals.

issues.description: Private oracle file is well-isolated under evaluation/private/ and not part of participant-facing artifacts, so no leak to participants, but worth noting it duplicates constants also embedded directly in evaluate.py (redundant but harmless).

recommendations: Consider softening or removing the netlist comment '// secure_enable is driven directly by a constant-tie cell.' to reduce the direct hint toward the anomaly location, relying instead on participants discovering this via structural analysis as intended by the README's framing.

Optionally add an explicit false_positive_rate and inference_latency computation/emission in evaluate.py (or document that these are computed by an external harness wrapping evaluate.py) so the metric-measurement chain is fully traceable end-to-end.
